commands: python3 -c "<digest-match sweep of .agent-harness/runs and docs for raw admission tokens>"

findings.statement: Round-2 finding 1 (idempotent re-stop guard failed open via an `or result_sha` default, so a planted claim file yielded an accepted result with no attribution record) is FIXED in the committed bytes. subagent_stop_validate.py:395-408 now blocks on the same-agent re-claim path unless the receipt state is exactly 'consumed' AND the recorded result_sha256 equals the freshly computed digest; there is no defaulting expression anywhere in the file (grep for result_sha256 returns only lines 403, 430, 445, none of which supply a fallback). test_planted_claim_cannot_skip_attribution (test_hooks.py:1061) asserts the block, that the receipt stays 'open', and that no ledger file is created at all.
assumptions_used: The stop hook is the only writer of consumed receipts under the stated threat model.

findings.statement: Round-2 finding 2 (orphan receipt when the ledger append failed) is FIXED for the reported path. admit_agent.py:191-217 appends the 'minted' ledger row first and only then writes the receipt, and fails closed on OSError, so no receipt can outlive a failed mint. test_admit_agent_fails_closed_when_ledger_cannot_be_written (test_hooks.py:1102) chmods the run directory 0o500, asserts a non-zero exit with 'ledger could not be appended', and asserts the receipt file does not exist. The same ordering discipline was NOT applied to the consume side; see F-R3-11.

Round-2 finding 3 (result artifact read twice, so validated bytes could differ from digested bytes) is FIXED. subagent_stop_validate.py:338-346 performs one resolved.read_bytes(), parses the object from those bytes via decode, and computes result_sha from the same buffer. The identical single-read discipline is applied to the assignment at lines 156-168 (assignment_raw -> json.loads(assignment_raw.decode) -> recomputed_sha). No second read of either path exists in the file.

Round-2 finding 4 (ledger never validated and gitignored) is FIXED as claimed, with two scope gaps recorded separately. validate_harness.py:194-239 walks every consumed receipt, requires a runs/<run>/ADMISSIONS.jsonl, and compares result_sha256, token_digest, and the writing agent (row.agent_id vs receipt.consumed_by_agent_id). Ledgers are tracked despite `/.agent-harness/runs/` being gitignored (.gitignore:62): `git ls-files '*ADMISSIONS.jsonl'` returns three force-added ledgers, including the D-067 canary run. Gaps: the cross-check is one-directional (a ledger 'consumed' row with no matching consumed receipt is never flagged) and it skips consumed receipts whose runs/<run> directory does not exist (see F-R3-10, F-R3-14).

Round-2 finding 5 (a live run wedged by the result-to-receipt rule before Stop was dispatched) is FIXED as described. validate_harness.py:171-186 reports a result whose receipt is still 'open' under `pending_results` and continues, instead of appending an error; the field is emitted in the ok:true payload at lines 244-255. Confirmed live: probe P1 shows `"pending_results": ["A-HOOK-FIXTURE"]` with ok:true while the receipt is open. This fix is correct for the reported symptom but is the enabling half of the new defect in F-R3-10.

Round-2 finding 6 (`??` porcelain entries misreported as tracked modifications) is FIXED. validate_harness.py:136-140 filters out lines beginning with '??' before turning the remainder into 'Tracked run evidence modified after commit' errors. Probes P1/P3/P4/P5/P6 all ran in fresh `git init` sandboxes whose entire .agent-harness/runs tree is untracked and none produced a tracked-evidence error.

Round-2 finding 7 (two false claims in the admit_agent.py docstring about token secrecy) is FIXED and the scrubber exists and was actually run. admit_agent.py:19-39 now states plainly that the token does not stay secret, that it appears in any transcript or captured stop-event JSON, that a captured BLOCKED stop is the dangerous case because the receipt is still open, and it carries an explicit THREAT MODEL paragraph. scrub_admission_proof.py exists and the retained canary stop-event JSONs are scrubbed: stop_event_d067-canary-c1/c2-substitution/c3-leasefail all carry `"admission_proof": "sha256:..."`. A digest-match sweep of every 20-64 char token-like string in .agent-harness/runs and docs against all 8 known token_digests found exactly one live raw token, in run-20260729-f10-d067-review-r2/results/A-D067-REVIEW-R2.json, which is precisely the residual the audit report discloses in section 5, and whose receipt is 'consumed' (spent). The disclosure is accurate. Coverage gap recorded in F-R3-12.
assumptions_used: secrets.token_urlsafe(32) tokens are 43 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-], which the sweep regex covers.
reproduction: digest-match sweep: hash every [A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,64} substring under .agent-harness/runs and docs, compare to all token_digest values

findings.statement: Round-2 finding 8 (concurrency test ran nothing concurrently) is FIXED. test_concurrent_stops_consume_receipt_once (test_hooks.py:1015-1058) spawns four Popen children, writes the payload to and closes every child's stdin in one loop (lines 1037-1040) before reading any stdout (lines 1042-1045), so the children genuinely overlap. Its invariant is the right one: exactly one 'consumed' ledger row, every non-empty stdout a block, at least one empty stdout. It passes in the 35/35 run.

Round-2 finding 9 (the ACTIVE_RUN bypass merely relocated to deleting CONTEXT_INDEX.json) is FIXED as claimed. subagent_stop_validate.py:82-93 now judges 'harness installed' from `harness.is_dir()` -- the .agent-harness directory itself -- not from any single file inside it, and test_stop_blocks_when_active_run_is_deleted (test_hooks.py:1229) covers the ACTIVE_RUN deletion case. The keying is correct for the file-deletion class. The bypass does, however, relocate once more to how the harness directory is located at all; see F-R3-13.

NEW defect introduced by the second fix pass: `admit_agent.py --reopen` silently clears the post-hoc-edit detector for a result that was already admitted. Reproduced end to end (probe P1). Sequence: agent stops and is accepted; validate_harness reports ok:true. The result artifact is then edited in place; validate_harness correctly reports ok:false with 'Result artifact changed after it was admitted'. Running `admit_agent.py --assignment-id <id> --reopen --reason ...` then flips the receipt back to state 'open', and the very next validate_harness run reports ok:true with `pending_results: ["A-HOOK-FIXTURE"]` -- against the same edited bytes. The mechanism is the interaction of the round-2 fix for finding 5 (an open receipt makes a result 'pending', not an error, validate_harness.py:176-181) with the reopen lifecycle (admit_agent.py:150-186), plus the absence of any reverse ledger->receipt reconciliation. The ledger does retain the earlier 'consumed' row and a 'minted' row with reopened:true (probe P8), so the event is forensically recoverable, but the validator -- the single automated check the D-067 report cites as detecting 'the D-066 incident class' -- returns ok:true. Reopen requires only ACTIVE_RUN, a non-stale assignment, and a --reason string, all of which an agent with exec_command can supply.
assumptions_used: An adjudicator or CI reads the validator's ok field; pending_results is informational and does not change the exit code.
reproduction: observe: ok:false after the edit, then ok:true with pending_results after --reopen
unresolved: Suggested repair: treat a run whose ledger holds a 'consumed' row for an assignment whose receipt is now 'open' as an error, or record the last consumed result_sha256 in reopened_from and keep enforcing it.

findings.statement: NEW defect: the ordering discipline that round-2 finding 2 imposed on the mint side was not applied to the consume side, producing the mirror-image orphan. subagent_stop_validate.py:420-453 writes the consumed receipt FIRST and appends the ledger row second, inside one try. Reproduced (probe P5): with the run directory made read-only, the stop is blocked with 'Admission receipt could not be consumed (PermissionError)' -- but the receipt on disk is already state='consumed' with result_sha256 recorded, and no ledger file exists. The agent's retry then takes the idempotent same-agent path (lines 384-409), matches the recorded digest, and is ACCEPTED with empty stdout, and the ledger row is still never written even though the directory is writable again. validate_harness does catch the end state ('Consumed receipt has no admission ledger'), so the system is fail-closed at validation time, but the Stop hook itself reports acceptance for a result with no durable attribution -- which is exactly the property the D-065 obligation names.
unresolved: Suggested repair: append the ledger row before writing the consumed receipt, mirroring admit_agent.py, or make the idempotent path repair a missing ledger row.

findings.statement: NEW/residual defect in the scrubber's coverage, silently. scrub_admission_proof.py only processes files that json.loads successfully (line 94-96 swallows every failure with `continue`) and --run only globs '*.json' (line 87). Probe P2 planted the same token five ways under a run's raw_logs and ran `--run`: the normal event JSON and a whitespace-padded key were scrubbed, but the token SURVIVED in (a) a twice-escaped payload -- a JSON file storing the whole stop event as a JSON *string*, where the regex at line 69 fails because the character after `admission_proof` is a backslash, not a quote; (b) a .log transcript; (c) a .md note. The tool then prints 'total tokens scrubbed: 2' with no indication that three files still carry the secret. Real .log and .txt files are retained under .agent-harness/runs today (e.g. run-.../raw_logs/*.log), so the shape is not hypothetical. No live leak exists in the current repository -- the digest-match sweep in F-R3-07 found only the one already-disclosed spent token -- so this is a latent coverage gap, not a present exposure.
unresolved: Suggested repair: scrub all retained files as text, count non-JSON and unparseable files, and report them instead of skipping silently.

findings.statement: NEW defect: the Stop hook fails OPEN in exactly the condition for which validate_harness.py was hardened to fail CLOSED. validate_harness.py:126-131 appends an error when git cannot be run ('an unrunnable integrity check is not a passed one'). The Stop hook resolves the repository through _common.repo_root() (_common.py:27-38), which shells out to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and, on FileNotFoundError, falls back to Path.cwd(). If git is absent or broken and the hook's cwd is not the repository root, `harness.is_dir()` at subagent_stop_validate.py:86 is False and the hook returns at line 93 with exit 0 and empty stdout -- i.e. ACCEPT, with no lease, receipt, envelope, or contract check performed at all. Reproduced (probe P9): PATH stripped of git, cwd set to a subdirectory, valid harness present at the real root, result ACCEPTED with rc 0 and empty output. Under the recorded LOCAL-ADAPT the parent invokes the hook with cwd at the repo root and git is installed, so this is latent, not live; but it is the same 'harness installed' bypass class as round-2 finding 9, relocated from ACTIVE_RUN to CONTEXT_INDEX.json to root resolution.
assumptions_used: The hook's cwd and PATH are set by the runtime, not by the subagent.
unresolved: Suggested repair: block when repo_root() had to fall back, or search upward for .agent-harness instead of trusting cwd.

findings.statement: NEW defect (minor): the ledger cross-check iterates run directories, not receipts, so a consumed receipt filed under a run id with no .agent-harness/runs/<id> directory is never cross-checked. validate_harness.py:198-202 builds run_receipts by filtering `consumed` on run_dir.name, so receipts for a missing run directory simply never appear in any iteration. Reproduced (probe P6): a planted consumed receipt at admissions/run-ghost/A-GHOST.json produced ok:true. Exploit value is low because deleting the run directory also deletes the results being attributed, but it is an unchecked path in a check whose stated scope is 'every consumed receipt'. Two legitimate states were confirmed NOT to false-positive: a run directory with no receipts and no ledger (probe P4, ok:true) and a reopened receipt consumed a second time by a different agent, producing two ledger consume rows (probe P3, ok:true, last row correctly matched).

The agent_id half of the D-065 obligation ('bind one spawned agent_id to one run, assignment, and digest') is enforced only by operator convention, not by the tooling. admit_agent.py:84-89 defaults --expect-agent-id to the empty string, and subagent_stop_validate.py:236-242 skips the identity check entirely when it is empty, so a receipt minted without the flag admits ANY agent that holds the token. The docstring says 'Always pass --expect-agent-id' (admit_agent.py:24-27) but nothing warns or fails when it is omitted. Current practice is good: six of the eight receipts on disk carry expected_agent_id, including this assignment's ('d067-review-r3'); the two that do not are the pre-convention round-1 review receipts. Recommend making the flag required, or emitting a loud warning when it is absent.
reproduction: python3 -c "import json,glob; [print(json.load(open(p)).get('expected_agent_id'), p) for p in sorted(glob.glob('.agent-harness/admissions/*/*.json'))]"

findings.statement: The stated residual (shared OS user, deliberate forgery unprevented) is disclosed honestly, completely, and consistently on every surface that matters -- admit_agent.py:33-39, .agent-harness/README.md (the 'defeats confusion, races, and prompt-level substitution; it is not a defence against an agent that deliberately writes outside its declared result path' paragraph), FROZEN_DECISIONS.md row D-067, docs/harness/VALIDATION_LEDGER.md row 2026-07-29, and audit report sections 2 and 5, with no gate flip anywhere. Section 5 even discloses the one surviving raw token by name, and I independently confirmed it is real, is in the file named, and belongs to an already-consumed receipt. But three surfaces overclaim a DIFFERENT property, the one F-R3-10 breaks: audit report section 2, table row 'Fabricated or post-hoc edited result | invisible | validator error'; FROZEN_DECISIONS.md D-067, 'validate_harness.py requires every result to carry a consumed receipt whose digest still matches'; and VALIDATION_LEDGER.md 2026-07-29, 'validator negative control on a tampered admitted result'. All three state an unconditional guarantee that the same slice's own pending_results carve-out and reopen path make conditional. The residual is honest; this specific capability claim is not.
unresolved: Suggested repair: qualify the row as 'validator error while the receipt stays consumed', or close F-R3-10 and keep the row.

findings.statement: Live evidence and test count verified against the committed bytes. `git diff ed7bc49 HEAD -- .codex .agent-harness/scripts .agent-harness/tests` is empty, so the working tree under review is byte-identical to commit ed7bc49. `venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider .agent-harness/tests/test_hooks.py` gives 35 passed in 1.67s, matching the claimed 12 -> 35. Canary evidence confirmed: C1 stop_out is empty (ACCEPT) and the ledger carries its attribution row (agent_id d067-canary-c1, result_sha256 sha256:0e7b3cac..., token_digest matching the mint row); C2 substitution stop_out is a block with 'admission_proof does not match the receipt for A-D067-CANARY-C2-VICTIM'; C3 stop_out is a block with 'No Start-time run lease exists for this agent ... Refusing to fall back to the mutable ACTIVE_RUN pointer'. The ledger holds 7 rows: 2 legacy consumes with no mint row (minted before the ledger-first ordering existed), 3 mints, 2 consumes; the victim receipt is correctly absent from the consumes and remains 'open'. All four D-065 obligation items have a concrete implementation and a fixture: same-run substitution (test_hooks.py:730), receipt/ledger-write failure (1102), lease-write failure (853), live overlapping-run canary with unique write attribution (C1).

ADJUDICATION SUMMARY for D-070. Against the current committed bytes (ed7bc49) and the explicitly stated threat model, the D-065 obligation is PARTIALLY DISCHARGED. All nine round-2 findings are genuinely fixed in the current bytes, not merely claimed (F-R3-01..F-R3-09), and all four obligation clauses have real implementations, real negative fixtures, and a passing live overlapping-run canary with unique write attribution (F-R3-17). Clause 1 (atomic binding) is delivered by the parent-minted receipt plus the O_EXCL claim, with the caveat that the agent_id component is optional in the tool (F-R3-15). Clauses 2, 3, and 4 are fully delivered. What blocks a full discharge is that the second fix pass introduced a new defect in the exact capability the obligation depends on: `--reopen` clears the result-to-digest binding for an already-admitted result, so a post-hoc edited artifact validates ok:true (F-R3-10, reproduced end to end). Two further fail-open paths were introduced or left in place -- the consume-side ledger orphan (F-R3-11) and the Stop hook's silent accept when the repo root cannot be resolved (F-R3-13). None of these three require the residual (deliberate out-of-path writing); they are confusion-class and environment-class failures, which is precisely the class D-067 claims to remove. Recommendation: do not flip G-HARNESS-INTEGRITY on these bytes. F-R3-10 is a small, well-scoped fix; with it and F-R3-11 closed and the three surfaces in F-R3-16 requalified, the obligation would be dischargeable without further redesign.
assumptions_used: The threat model as written is accepted: no defence against an agent deliberately writing outside its declared result path.
unresolved: Whether PARTIALLY DISCHARGED is sufficient for a gate flip is D-070's call, not this review's.
